slides.texte_overlay:
How to keep your cool
when things go wrong
Slow your breathing first. Four seconds in, six seconds out. Your body calms down before your mind does. Repeat three times.
Name the problem in one sentence. "The flight is cancelled." Putting it simply makes it feel smaller and easier to solve.
Ask what you can control right now. Rebook, call, wait, eat. Acting on one small thing stops the feeling of chaos.
Keep your voice low and slow. Even when others raise theirs. Calm is contagious, and people start following your lead.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A broader view of the world makes daily problems feel smaller.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A broader view of the world makes daily problems feel smaller.

slides.texte_overlay: Find something to laugh about. Humour in bad moments relaxes everyone, including you. A light joke can turn a disaster into a story you'll tell for years.
Look back afterwards. What went well, what you'd change. Each hard moment prepares you for the next one. You get calmer every time.
